subtitle: Cross-reading for 3 September 2026: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) price from the confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 15:22 BRT (18:22 UTC), presidential book at USD 142.35M, against the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp), the only national poll with published figures this Thursday. Its release was already on the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) register that the panel ingested that same morning. ⭐ IT FLIPS THE [SECOND ROUND](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) WITHIN ITS OWN HOUSE: Flávio Bolsonaro 45% and Lula 44%, after Lula 46% to 45% on 13/Aug and Lula 45% to 44% on 27/Aug. ⚠️ AND THE HOUSE FROM THE DAY BEFORE MEASURED THE OPPOSITE in the same pairing: Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of 02/Sep, with an overlapping field window, gave Lula ahead by 42% to 41%. Two other national polls had releases scheduled for this Thursday on the TSE register, [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) and 100 Cidades, and neither had published figures at the time of this reading.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 54.50% (vol USD 9.63M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 15:22 BRT (18:22 UTC). Down 1.00pp, after five days flat at 55.50%. POLL: the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp) gives him 37% in the first round and 44% in a second round in which the runner-up has 45%. He wins the other three pairings the house tested: 44% to 42% against Ronaldo Caiado, 44% to 42% against Romeu Zema and 44% to 39% against Renan Santos.
fortes: He is still ahead in the first round, with 37% against 34% for the runner-up, and the 3-point gap is the same one PoderData itself measured on 27/Aug.
He wins three of the four second-round pairings the house tested, two of them by 2 points and one by 5.
In the first-round runner-up contract he rose 0.75pp and now stands at 8.75%, in a contract of USD 437 thousand.
The fall in his price this round came alongside the runner-up's, and not with a rise from his opponent as it did the day before.
This Thursday, at 3pm at the Planalto Palace, he held the ceremony at which he declared the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) queue cleared, according to Poder360.
fracos: ⚠️ FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE THREE ROUNDS FROM THIS HOUSE SINCE 13/Aug he appears behind in the second round against the runner-up, 44% to 45%, after 46% to 45% on 13/Aug and 45% to 44% on 27/Aug.
In the price he gave up 1.00pp and stands at 54.50%, ending the run of five days without a move.
In the first round he gave ground within the house for the second round running, from 41% on 13/Aug to 38% on 27/Aug and 37% now.

The INSS ceremony uses a stated criterion that narrows what the announcement means: the queue counts as cleared when applications still inside the legal review deadline stop counting as pending, and the count excludes those waiting outside that criterion, according to O Globo.
The government approval reading is still the Quaest one of 02/Sep, with 45% approval against 48% disapproval, because PoderData did not publish approval figures in the table that was checked.
candidates.analise: Thursday brought one national poll with published figures, and it measures almost the same week as Wednesday's national poll, offset by a day. In the first round his position gives ground again within the house, from 38% to 37%, and the gap to the runner-up stays flat at 3 points. What really changes is the second round: for the first time in the three rounds from this house since 13/Aug he appears behind, 44% to 45%. The house from the day before measured the same pairing the other way, 42% to 41% in his favour, and both gaps are 1 point against a declared margin of 2pp. The panel does not say which of the two is right: it records that the pairing that decides the election no longer has a stable sign across houses. In the price, his move was a fall for the first time in six days, and the gap to the runner-up narrowed even with the runner-up also falling, because he fell further.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 40.35% (vol USD 9.59M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 15:22 BRT (18:22 UTC). Down 0.30pp, on the same day the leader also fell, and the gap between the two went from 14.85pp to 14.15pp. POLL: the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp) gives him 34% in the first round and 45% in a second round against the leader, who has 44%.
fortes: ⭐ IN THE SECOND ROUND HE APPEARS NUMERICALLY AHEAD FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THE THREE ROUNDS FROM THIS HOUSE SINCE 13/Aug, 45% to 44%, after 45% to 46% on 13/Aug and 44% to 45% on 27/Aug.
His gap to the leader in the house's first round went from 6 points on 13/Aug to 3 on 27/Aug and stayed at 3 now.
In the first-round runner-up contract he remains dominant and did not move, at 85.50% in a contract of USD 519 thousand.
His fall in the price was 0.30pp, against 1.00pp for the leader, meaning he lost less than his opponent on the same day.
fracos: In the first round he gave ground within the house, from 35% on 13/Aug and 35% on 27/Aug to 34% now.
In the price he fell 0.30pp and stands at 40.35%, and the 1.70pp rise of the day before did not carry through.

The 1-point lead in the second round sits inside the declared margin of 2pp, meaning it is a statistical tie by the house's own yardstick, and the house from the day before measured the same pairing the other way.
He used the crisis at the Supreme Court to try to build momentum for the 7 September rally, according to Folha de S.Paulo, on a day when the news agenda sat with the court rather than the campaign.
candidates.analise: His day is the inverse of yesterday's in both measurements. In declared voting intention he posted his own series' best result in the pairing that decides the election, appearing numerically ahead for the first time in the three rounds from this house since 13/Aug. In the first round, however, he gave up 1 point within the same house and the gap to the leader stayed flat at 3. In the price he fell, and he fell on the same day the leader fell further, so the gap between the two narrowed without him rising. It is the second reading in a row in which price and declared voting intention point in different directions, and this time with the signs swapped relative to the day before.

fortes: The margin against him in the second round narrowed within the house, from 7 points on 27/Aug to 5 now, with him going from 37% to 39%.
He is the only one of the names outside the top two that PoderData tests in a second round and who improved his own position between the house's two rounds.
He filed for the impeachment of two Supreme Court justices in the Senate, according to Poder360, and with that he remains inside the story dominating the week's news.
Accumulated volume in his winner contract is still the largest among the lower-polling names, at USD 12.48M.

In the first round he gave ground within the house, from 4% on 27/Aug to 3%, over the same interval in which Augusto Cury went from 4% to 10%.
In the first-round third-place contract the gap to the leader doubled in size over two days, and he stands at 27.00% against 55.85%.
He has the largest accumulated volume among the lower-polling names and even so his price stands at 1.75%, meaning big money did not hold up the price.
candidates.analise: His week carries two opposite signals and the contracts have to be kept apart. In declared voting intention he gave ground in the first round within the house, from 4% to 3%, over exactly the interval in which Augusto Cury went from 4% to 10% at the same institute. In the second round against the leader, though, he improved: the margin fell from 7 to 5 points within the house. In the price the reading is one of decline in both contracts, and the bigger loss is in the third-place contract, where he was overtaken on 01/Sep and the gap to the leader has doubled since. His winner contract holds the largest accumulated volume among the lower-polling names, at USD 12.48M, and even so the price does not go beyond 1.75%.

candidates.subtitle: Trailing pack at the confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 15:22 BRT (18:22 UTC), and this Thursday what changes is the third reading in a row of the same second-round pairing. Ronaldo Caiado went from 4% to 2% within PoderData itself, between 27/Aug and now, and in the second round he sits 2 points behind the leader, 44% to 42%. Over three days that pairing was measured by three houses with overlapping field windows and produced three results: 45% to 43% in his favour at Real Time Big Data on 01/Sep, 42% to 37% against him at Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep and 44% to 42% against him now.

caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), 0.25% (vol USD 7.11M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round does not publish a new price for him in that contract. In the first-round THIRD-PLACE contract, which is a different market, he rose 2.50pp and stands at 11.00%, in a book of 111 thousand dollars accumulated. IN THIS THURSDAY'S DECLARED VOTING INTENTION HE LOSES THE SECOND ROUND TO THE LEADER BY 44% TO 42%, the smallest margin against him among the week's three houses.
caiado.fortes: His 2.50pp rise in the first-round third-place contract is the panel's largest upward move this round, and it more than recovers the 4.50pp fall of the day before. In the PoderData second round he sits 2 points behind the leader, 44% to 42%, against 3 points in the same house's round of 27/Aug. He argued for Alexandre de Moraes to be removed from the case and for impeachment in the Senate, according to Valor Econômico, and for the Supreme Court to lift secrecy on every investigation into Banco Master, INSS and Dark Horse, according to Estadão.
caiado.fracos: In the first round he fell from 4% to 2% within PoderData itself, between 27/Aug and now. In the winner contract he remains below the 0.5% floor, and this round does not publish a new price for him there. And the second-round pairing he appears in has already been measured three different ways in three days, which makes any single reading of it fragile.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), 0.05% (vol USD 7.43M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round does not publish a new price for him. He is not a presidential candidate: he is running for governor of São Paulo.
haddad.fortes: He is not tested as a presidential candidate in the national polls of the window, so there is no ballot reading to cross against the price.
haddad.fracos: The contract remains open under his name by inheritance of the market's design, not by a declared candidacy, and the panel keeps the line only so the residual price is not read as a signal.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), 0.15% (vol USD 6.51M) in the WINNER contract, below the 0.5% floor of the double reading, and this round does not publish a new price for him in that contract. In the first-round THIRD-PLACE contract, which is a different market, he stands at 0.80%, in a book of 49 thousand dollars accumulated.
zema.fortes: In the PoderData second round he sits 2 points behind the leader, 44% to 42%, by far his best result among the week's three houses and the smallest margin against him in any national poll in the window.
zema.fracos: He has 1% in the first round, against 2% in the same house's round of 27/Aug. And the second round against the leader is the scenario in which the week's three houses disagree most: Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep gave 44% to 33%, a margin of 11 points, Real Time Big Data of 01/Sep gave 43% to 40%, a margin of 3, and PoderData now gives 44% to 42%, a margin of 2. Three houses, three margins, over three days.

candidates.analise: The second-round pairing against Ronaldo Caiado is the portrait of the week: three houses, three results, all with overlapping field windows. Real Time Big Data of 01/Sep gave him ahead of the leader by 45% to 43%, Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep gave the leader ahead by 42% to 37%, and PoderData of 03/Sep gives the leader ahead by 44% to 42%. The margins range from 2 points behind to 5 points ahead, within a span of three days. The panel records all three readings and does not choose between them. In the first round, at the same time, he gave ground within PoderData itself, from 4% on 27/Aug to 2%. In the price all three remain below the floor in the winner contract, and the only publishable move is Caiado's in the third-place contract, which rose 2.50pp and stands at 11.00%, the panel's largest upward move this round.
candidates.fortes: Ronaldo Caiado rose 2.50pp in the first-round third-place contract, the panel's largest upward move this round, and in the PoderData second round he sits 2 points behind the leader, the smallest gap the house has ever measured in that pairing.
candidates.fracos: None of the three reaches 3% in the PoderData first round, all three remain below the 0.5% floor in the winner contract, and Caiado gave ground within the house, from 4% on 27/Aug to 2% now.

quadroComparativo.s: The Prosecutor General's Office closed a plea agreement with Antonio Carlos Freixo Júnior, owner of Entre Investimentos, the first cooperation deal tied directly to the Dark Horse case, according to Folha de S.Paulo and O Globo, and the agreement has not yet been ratified. On 02/Sep the same office signed the plea deal of João Carlos Mansur, founder of Reag, and sent it to André Mendonça's chambers for ratification, according to Poder360 and G1. Gilmar Mendes proposed to Edson Fachin that Federal Police officers be barred from the court's chambers, according to Folha de S.Paulo. The Paraná bar association asked for Moraes to be removed from the case and for the prosecutor general to be recused, according to Folha de S.Paulo. Mendonça's report on Moraes is still expected on 7 or 8 September, according to Poder360.

cruzamento: 3 September is the round in which two houses measured almost identical weeks and disagreed about who wins the second round between the top two. In declared voting intention, the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp) gives Flávio Bolsonaro 45% and Lula 44%, with 8% blank or spoiled and 3% don't know. In the same house's two previous rounds it was the leader ahead, by 46% to 45% on 13/Aug and by 45% to 44% on 27/Aug, and this is the first of the three rounds from this house since 13/Aug in which the runner-up appears numerically ahead in that pairing. The gap is 1 point and the declared margin is 2pp, meaning a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) by the house's own yardstick. Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep, with a field window of 30/Aug to 01/Sep that overlaps almost entirely with this one, measured the same pairing the other way, 42% to 41% in the leader's favour, also with a 1-point gap. The panel records both readings and does not choose between them: what the week shows is that the pairing of the top two no longer has a stable sign across houses. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) PoderData gives the leader 37% and the runner-up 34%, and within the house itself the gap went from 6pp on 13/Aug to 3pp on 27/Aug and stayed at 3pp now. Augusto Cury's jump is confirmed by a second house: 4% on 27/Aug and 10% now at PoderData, against 2% on 14/Aug and 10% on 02/Sep at Quaest. Two independent institutes are measuring the same direction within their own series. The second round against Ronaldo Caiado already has three different results in the same week, all with overlapping field windows: PoderData gives the leader ahead by 44% to 42%, Quaest gave 42% to 37% and Real Time Big Data of 01/Sep gave Caiado ahead by 45% to 43%. In the price, the fact of the day is that the top two fell together, which did not happen in the previous round. The leader gave up 1.00pp and stands at 54.50%, after five days flat, and the runner-up gave up 0.30pp and stands at 40.35%. The gap between them narrowed for the second day running, from 16.55pp on 01/Sep to 14.85pp on 02/Sep and 14.15pp now, but for a different reason than yesterday: yesterday the runner-up rose, today the leader fell further. The sum of the YES legs in the presidential book stands at 99.20%, meaning the price that left the top two did not reappear under another name. Augusto Cury remains the clearest case of different contracts answering different questions: in the winner contract he fell 0.25pp and stands at 1.35%, and in the first-round third-place contract he rose 3.45pp and now stands at 55.85%, a second straight day of gains. The contract on a Supreme Court justice leaving through impeachment before 2027 rose 1.05pp and stands at 7.40%, the third direction in a row over three days after 10.85% and 6.35%, with accumulated volume flat at USD 87 thousand. A price that moves a lot on very little money does not describe a shift in expectations of the same size.
